# Content, attribution and modifications

The selected Wiktionnaire/Wiktionary contributor text and Lexique translations,
grammatical explanations, IPA presentation, selected-source excerpts and licensed
membership are distributed under **Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0
International**. The complete applicable licence and warranty disclaimer are in
[COPYING](COPYING); its public legal text is
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Adaptations retain downstream CC BY-SA rights. Application/converter code has
the separate MIT licence (`LICENSE-MIT` in the prepared resource).

Credit Wiktionnaire and Wiktionary contributors, and Lexique contributors for the
recorded selection/adaptations. Every field's fixed article/version and author
history are recorded in [curated-inputs.json](curated-inputs.json), with exact
selected lines in [selected-source-excerpts.json](selected-source-excerpts.json).
Credit Boris New and Christophe Pallier for Lexique 3.83 membership/frequencies,
retaining the actual corpus contributors and source statements in
[LEXIQUE-UPSTREAM-README.txt](LEXIQUE-UPSTREAM-README.txt),
[lexique-provenance.json](lexique-provenance.json), and
[MEMBERSHIP-NOTICES.txt](MEMBERSHIP-NOTICES.txt).

Modifications by Lexique: selected one specified use per frozen
group; removed wiki markup; added selected IPA slash delimiters; translated or
adapted scoped French, English and Chinese explanations; clarified auxiliary +
past-participle construction, all pronominal forms with être and verbs requiring
être rather than avoir; retained compound-tense anteriority including future
reference times; clarified article/pronoun agreement, elision, complement and
register restrictions; distinguished the whole/entire adjective from the
distributive indefinite adjective and the adverb; retained the psychoanalytic
domain of the noun ça; and bound the four evidenced source spellings. Each field
records its own actual modification. The membership projects four accepted
columns and preserves NFC spelling, original POS, frequency values and row order.

Article-level `Import:DAF8` and other supplied source/reference notices are retained
in [selected-source-context.json](selected-source-context.json). They do not
admit unselected DAF8/TLFi bodies. The cœur/coeur contributor merger at revision
1507043 has distinct fixed article/history and older merger-context records;
credit is not reduced to the one early editor. Historical evidence identifies
authorship/source boundaries separately from current selected content. No whole
page or corpus licensing conclusion is asserted.

The elected CC BY-SA route follows [Wikimedia Terms revision 598588](https://foundation.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=Policy:Terms_of_Use&oldid=598588):
§7(a) contributor licensing; §7(g) reuse, attribution and imported-source notices;
§7(h) modification/addition and licensing notices. French/English contributor
policies and selected-source boundary evidence remain in the context records.
GFDL is not additionally imposed. CC BY-SA does not require the whole upstream
corpus or executable corresponding source; this core bundles its actual curated
inputs, converter, selected excerpts and notices for reproducibility.

The independently accepted auxiliary explanations express grammar facts
corroborated by [OQLF](https://vitrinelinguistique.oqlf.gouv.qc.ca/24224/la-grammaire/le-verbe/auxiliaires/emploi-des-auxiliaires-avoir-et-etre).
The adjective distinction for tout is corroborated by the
[Canadian Translation Bureau](https://nos-langues.canada.ca/fr/cles-de-la-redaction/tout-accord-de-ladjectif),
with the frozen grammatical subclasses defined by the
[Lexique 3 manual](https://www.lexique.org/databases/Lexique382/Manuel_Lexique3.html).
OQLF and Canadian Translation Bureau prose is excluded. Exact accepted texts,
usages and grammar-fact evidence are in [field-review.json](field-review.json).
The project owner's approved #81 scope includes `ça/NOM` as that batch's specialist
exception, retaining its psychoanalytic, masculine, singular and uncountability
restrictions. It is counted separately from everyday coverage. Learner acceptance
remains unrun.

## Batch 002 (#82)

The batch adds 47 independently reviewed groups and reuses `bien/ADV` and
`bien/NOM` unchanged. All new field adaptations, selected excerpts and grammatical
restrictions retain CC BY-SA 4.0, their fixed versions/spans, contributor histories
and individual modification notices. The three new spelling records use fixed
hard redirects for `t'` → `t’` and `s'` → `s’`; `s'` keeps distinct conjunction
and personal-pronoun records. They produce two additional query aliases.

Also credit **Académie française, Dictionnaire de l’Académie française,
8th edition (1932–1935)** for the declared import notices on `pouvoir`, `nous`,
`moi`, `devoir`, `oui`, `comme`, `venir` and `sur`. The independent batch review
distinguishes surviving selected wording from article-level import credit and
separately records historical revisions and the combined redistribution
obligations in [selected-source-context.json](selected-source-context.json).
Older authorship evidence does not replace the selected fixed content revision.

Frozen `où/PRO:int` corresponds to the selected source's interrogative adverb;
`où/PRO:rel` corresponds to its relative adverb. The terminology is corroborated
by [OQLF's classification of où](https://vitrinelinguistique.oqlf.gouv.qc.ca/21461/la-grammaire/les-pronoms/pronoms-relatifs/ou-employe-comme-pronom-relatif-ou-adverbe),
which also calls relative `où` a pronoun. These grammatical facts are paraphrased;
OQLF prose is excluded. The ordinary masculine, invariable letter name for
`y/NOM` is separately corroborated by
[Académie française](https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A9Y0001);
the modern article supplies corroboration only.

Frozen row 87, `quoi/ADJ`, remains a target with four unresolved fields.
The admitted pronoun uses retain their own subclasses and do not provide
adjective content. The owner's approved annotation exception completes #82 under
its amended scope with zero admitted fields for row 87. Its original curation,
review and incomplete machine coverage records remain unchanged. Complete D2
release acceptance remains open.

## Batch 003 (#83)

The batch adds fifty independently reviewed groups and 200 fields, selecting
one use per frozen row 0101–0150. Fixed Wiktionnaire revisions before
2026-10-01 00:00 UTC supply the selected contributor text and applicable IPA;
each field records its actual English/Chinese translation or explanatory
adaptation, selected-use restriction and original contributor history.
The selected/adapted fields and excerpts retain CC BY-SA 4.0. The
[source context](selected-source-context.json) and
[independent field review](field-review.json)
document the selected spans, authorship boundaries and redistribution route.

Also credit **Académie française, Dictionnaire de l’Académie française,
8th edition (1932–1935)** for the article-level import notices on `alors`, `aussi`,
`chose`, `jamais`, `même`, `penser`, `pourquoi`, `quand`, `sur` and `très`.
The context records distinguish these explicit `Import:DAF8` notices from
`R:DAF8` reference markers on other selected pages. Surviving selected imported
wording retains its own authorship and source boundaries; article-level notices
are retained even where the selected section predates or lies outside the import.
In particular, the selected `sur/PRE` definition and contributor example predate
the DAF8 import, which added adjective material. Older revision evidence does
not replace the fixed selected revision.

The adverbial `bon` is restricted to literal `sentir bon`, using the selected
licensed phrase definition. `petit/ADV` is restricted to writing in small
characters (`écrire petit`). TLFi/Robert classifications corroborate these uses;
their prose is excluded. Frozen `pourquoi/CON` and `comment/CON` correspond to
indirect subordination by interrogative adverbs, corroborated by
[OQLF](https://vitrinelinguistique.oqlf.gouv.qc.ca/fiche-gdt/fiche/26560285/adverbe-interrogatif);
they retain the frozen subclasses without relabelling the modern lexemes as
conjunctions. Grammar-fact corroboration is paraphrased; OQLF prose is excluded.

`même/PRO:ind` uses the clean fixed `le même` definition and form table, with
applicable IPA from `même`. The Reverso-cited pronoun section is excluded.
The Alexandria citation belongs to the unselected noun section; it is not
the source of the selected adjective or adverb. The article-level Académie
notice remains in the context. Literary quotations and older XMLittré
CC BY-SA 3.0 candidates are excluded from the new fields; that licence is not
relabelled as CC BY-SA 4.0.

The owner's approved #83 scope admits `par/NOM` as a specific specialist
exception: the conventional number of strokes required to complete a single
golf hole. Its masculine noun, golf domain and standard-stroke-count restrictions
remain in the selected fields and usage. The achieved score, Georgian-letter
name and preposition are excluded. This group is accepted separately from
literal everyday coverage, alongside the existing #81 exception.

## Batches #84–#89

The resource admits 296 additional groups / 1,184 fields, preserving the original
154 groups / 616 fields and counting reused rows 360, 422 and 423 once. Fixed
Wiktionnaire and English Wiktionary contributor spans, scoped Lexique translations
and grammatical explanations retain **CC BY-SA 4.0**, full contributor histories,
individual modification notices, applicable source/import credits and the warranty
disclaimer in [COPYING](COPYING). The actual import and bibliography markers and
their version/line boundaries are retained in [selected-source-context.json](selected-source-context.json).
Credit **Académie française, Dictionnaire de l’Académie française, huitième édition
(1932–1935)** wherever the supplied DAF8 import is declared. A bibliography marker
does not grant rights to an unselected publisher's prose. Protected dictionary
definitions, quotations, media and full-page captures are excluded.

The three beau/NOM prose fields adapt **Théodore Soulice (1800–1878), Petit
dictionnaire de la langue française, à l’usage des écoles primaires**, first edition
1836, Paris: **L. Hachette / Firmin Didot frères**, printed p. 56 / scan p. 62.
The selected original noun clause is public domain. Credit Wikisource transcription
contributors through the fixed page revision **14772408**, lines **142–143**, and
its complete history, recorded in the field source/context. Selection ends before
the semicolon introducing the separate **beau idéal** clause. The original printed
author/edition and the later transcription version remain distinct. Credit Lexique
contributors for the French adaptation and English/Chinese translations, including
the grammatical explanation. Reused transcription/adapted contributions follow the
elected CC BY-SA 4.0 route; the public-domain original does not acquire a ShareAlike
obligation merely by scanning or transcription. No author endorsement is implied.

Accurate scoped mappings retain their source category: English front adjective
supplies the semantic base for French avant/ADJ, with independent French grammar
facts and French IPA; French déjà/ADV supplies the reached-state meaning for the
reactive déjà/ONO use. The lowercase ok/ADJ and ok/ADV mappings use the attested
French **OK** source form; oeil/NOM uses the explicit typographic variant **œil**.
Regional familiar point/ADV selects the negative use after the finite verb without
ne. Usito, OQLF and modern Académie material corroborate usage facts only; their
proprietary explanatory text and examples are not redistributed.

All protected adapted contributions remain under CC BY-SA 4.0, with its attribution,
modification, ShareAlike, database and no-additional-restrictions obligations.
Applicable copyright, licence/disclaimer, import and previous-modification notices
are retained. The full/Lite dictionary inputs and notices are identical; application
and converter code remain separately MIT. The frozen denominator is 4,087 groups;
zero-field annotations at rows 87 and 305 are not admitted senses. The unchanged
specialist approvals at rows 34 and 128 retain their original restrictions.

## Content batches #90–#99

The additional 494 selected senses and 1,976 FR/IPA/EN/ZH fields retain their
exact fixed source versions, selected spans, original-author boundaries and
contributor histories in the accompanying inputs. Credit Lexique contributors
for each recorded scoped adaptation, translation and construction explanation.
The original Académie française eighth collective edition (1932–1935) is
public domain under the collective-work term; subsequent Wiktionnaire
contributor transcription/adaptation and Lexique adapted contributions retain
their separate CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution and ShareAlike obligations. The original
prose is not relabelled as CC-licensed. Unselected quotations and proprietary
corroboration prose are excluded. Bibliographic/import notices are retained
separately from admitted field text.

The complete development core contains 944 admitted groups / 3,776 fields,
942 everyday groups and two approved specialist senses. Seven owner-approved
annotations retain zero content and 28 missing fields. The 4,087-group /
3,773-headword denominator, original frequencies and existing learner data
remain unchanged. Full and Lite use identical dictionary content and notices.

## Content batches #100–#109

The additional 492 selected senses / 1,968 fields retain exact fixed sources, contributor histories and selected spans.
Credit Wiktionnaire and Wikisource contributors for source transcription/adaptation and Lexique contributors for recorded scoped adaptations, explanatory translations and construction notes, under CC BY-SA 4.0. The marché replacement retains the original 1836 Théodore Soulice public-domain source credit and its fixed Wikisource transcription separately from the recorded adaptations.
Where an Académie française eighth-edition marker is recorded, retain the original 1932–1935 collective edition credit and public-domain boundary, separately from subsequent CC BY-SA 4.0 contributions. Actual original authors/import and bibliography notices are retained in selected-source-context.json. Unselected quotation bodies, media and proprietary corroboration prose are excluded.
The current development core contains 1,436 admitted groups / 5,744 fields, 1,434 everyday groups, two specialist senses and 15 approved zero-field annotations / 60 missing fields. Full and Lite use identical dictionary content and notices.

## Batches #120–#129 sources and adaptations

Frozen rows 1951–2450 add 500 selected uses and 2,000 independently reviewed fields. All 1,935 previously admitted groups and fields remain unchanged. Modern meanings, pronunciation and register/construction restrictions are bound to each selected POS/use; individual adaptations and applicable historical source notices are recorded in the field and source context materials. Source spelling and capitalization bindings do not add runtime aliases.

## Modifications and attribution

Lexique contributors select one everyday use per group, adapt French lexical
definitions, author new English/Chinese explanations and select an applicable
isolated IPA variant. Construction, register, gender and number are retained.
EN/ZH are scoped explanations of the selected French semantics, rather than
upstream bilingual quotations. IPA notation does not include sound recordings.

Wiktionnaire contributors are credited through each complete linked article
history and the full named registry/returned anonymous counts in

revision and do not prove selected-sentence authorship. Lexique contributors
retain credit for selection, adaptations and explanatory translations.

## Selected boundaries and redistribution

`thème` selects exact topic/argument terms from lexical definition 10. The CFC cartography definition at
41 is excluded and supplies no field or rights claim. `automne` selects only
the first sentence of definition 12; the adjacent calendar/date claims are
excluded. The three supporting possessive articles establish the construction
of `miens` in `les miens`, while the exact `miens` page supplies its isolated IPA.
No runtime lookup alias is proposed. Longer original source prose is excluded
from current admission spans; [exact excerpts](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-140/source-excerpts.json) retain the
assessed units. Historical author/first-review snapshots and research captures
remain distinct from the current source selection.

Retain CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text and licence/source links, contributor/history
attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification notices and exact
selected spans. Share adaptations under CC BY-SA 4.0 without additional
restrictions. Unselected literary/news quotations, media, etymologies and
other-language content remain outside the field package. External works retain
their own rights. The coordinator verifies actual combined materials,
conversion and packaged notices before admission.

IPA variant is retained, with slashes added. Source spellings create no lookup aliases.

[Selected rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-141/selected-rights.md) explains the original collective-work basis.

## Redistribution obligations

Retain the licence text and identifiers, source/history links, contributor and applicable
original-work attribution, modification notices and selected source material. The adaptation
layer uses CC BY-SA 4.0 without additional restrictions. Referenced external works keep their
own rights; bibliography does not grant permission to redistribute their text. The coordinator
must verify the actual combined materials and notices before canonical admission.

All 200 selected fields pass independent quality and selected-text rights review.
Canonical conversion, actual packaged obligations and native checks remain pending.


# Source and modification notices for #142

Fixed Wiktionnaire contribution/transcription and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations retain
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-142/COPYING), fixed articles, complete linked histories,
contributor records and modifications accompany the independently reviewed proposals.

Exact word/POS membership and unchanged frequency strings derive from Boris New
and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, via the [frozen manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Rows 3051–3100 retain their order and subclasses; CEFR remains unknown.

## Modifications

French is scoped lexical adaptation. EN/ZH are new explanations of that same
use, not upstream bilingual quotations. IPA selects one applicable recorded
isolated variant and adds slashes; no audio is copied. Grammatical construction,
number, gender and register are retained. Media and attributed literary/news
sentences supply no learner field. Supporting source selections record exact lexical facts and construction/word forms. Source bindings add no runtime spelling alias.

## Article and original-work credits

Wiktionnaire contributors receive full article/history credit and the complete
named registry plus anonymous count in [source-context.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-142/source-context.json).
The current registry can include later editors; it does not prove selected
sentence authorship. Lexique contributors receive credit for selection,
adaptation and new explanatory text.

Twenty-nine articles have DAF8 import markers; `marrer` separately declares
Littré. Those historical originals retain their own credited rights, separate
from Wiktionnaire and Lexique adaptation/transcription. `carton`’s cartographic
CFC definition at line 53 is excluded from the packaging sense at line 26.
Referenced modern dictionaries and media receive no blanket licence inference.
External usage-check prose remains outside repository content.

## Current selected scope and delivery

196 fields / 49 groups pass quality and selected-expression rights.
Damoiseau/NOM row 3098 has zero selected fields and four missing annotation fields under the exact owner decision in owner-approval.json.
The developed source sentences for catastrophe, conscient, reproduire, affecter
are outside the selected redistribution packets. Exact limited lexical facts
and conventional short expressions are identified in source-excerpts.json,
with per-expression reasons in rights-fix-review.json. France expiry alone
does not clear whole original works in the US or worldwide.

The first review’s bavarder/témoignage Chinese corrections remain; all 12 affected learner texts are unchanged.
Retain complete CC BY-SA 4.0 text, attribution, version/history/contributor and
original-work credits, modification notices and the selected source materials.
The coordinator verifies the actual combined package before canonical admission.
The research archive and first-review snapshots supply evidence, not additional
selected dictionary text. Learner/native/release gates remain separate.


# Source and modification notices for #143

The fixed Wiktionnaire contribution layer and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations use
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code retains MIT. The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-143/COPYING), fixed
article links, full histories, contributor records and modification notices
accompany the reviewed shard.

Exact membership and both unchanged frequency strings derive from Boris New
and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
All rows 3101–3150, including `pars/NOM` and `uns/PRO:ind`, retain their identity
and order. CEFR remains unknown.

## Modifications

Fifty groups have one quality-reviewed selected sense and four fields each;
49 are everyday uses and `pars/NOM` is the approved specialist exception.
French definitions adapt the selected lexical semantics; EN/ZH are new Lexique
explanations, not upstream bilingual quotations. POS, construction, gender,
number, register and selected restrictions remain explicit. Applicable IPA
notation is retained; `chevalier` keeps its recorded optional-schwa notation.
The `uns` field isolates the recorded /œ̃/ segment of `les uns`, with the article
and liaison excluded, and retains the obligatory construction.
No source relation adds a runtime alias. [Exact proposals](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-143/review-candidates.md)
retain the 196 original fields and selected/excluded uses. The four approved
`pars/NOM` additions retain the exact proposal and accepted text in
[added fields](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-143/accepted-replacements.json). Original proposals remain in
[authored snapshot](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-143/authored/snapshot.json).

with their exact lines. [Selected rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-143/selected-rights.md) identifies the

conservative 2006-01-01 expiry. These declarations do not identify the author of
a selected sentence or authorize neighbouring external works.

work credits, licence and warranty notices, modification notices and CC BY-SA
4.0 for adaptations without additional restrictions. Preserve selected source
material and actual combined notices in the produced package. Literary/news
quotations, other-language content, media, audio, etymologies and unselected
external dictionary prose supply no learner field. Complete raw captures remain
in the external research archive, separately from redistribution inputs.

selected dictionary text. Learner/native/release gates remain separate.

frame; no bare-pronoun or lookup alias is admitted. Its IPA comes from the
fixed `sienne` form. `four électrique` supplies scoped cooking-appliance support.

Twenty-nine articles declare Académie française eighth-edition imports
(1932–1935). Original credit is retained separately from the wiki and Lexique
contribution/adaptation layers. [Selected rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-145/selected-rights.md) records
the established original collective-work basis and its 2006-01-01 expiry.
Historical original-work review does not review any new #145 field.
`symbole`'s CFC cartographic definition at line 21 is excluded; its general
representation definition at line 10 is selected. The unselected fifth-edition
Académie heraldry reference in `taré` supplies no proposed text.

## Redistribution obligations

Retain CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text and licence/source identifiers, complete
contributor/history attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification
notices and selected source material. Adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0 without
additional restrictions. External works retain their separate rights.
The coordinator verifies actual combined source materials, notices and
conversion before canonical admission.

All 200 fields have separate independent quality and selected-span rights
decisions. DAF8's France-only 2006-01-01 duration calculation does not establish
worldwide clearance of original expression. The accepted spans are assessed
individually as factual/conventional lexical material, and the full expressive
`terreur` proposal is not admitted. [Selected rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-145/selected-rights.md) and
[field-specific decisions](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-145/rights.json) identify this boundary separately from
CC BY-SA 4.0 contribution/adaptation obligations. Combined artifact delivery
and native validation remain pending with the coordinator.


# Source and modification notices for #146

The fixed Wiktionnaire contributions, scoped French adaptations and new
Lexique English/Chinese explanations retain [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
[COPYING](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-146/COPYING) supplies the legal text and warranty/liability disclaimer.
Project-owned code remains MIT. No endorsement by a source is implied.

Exact word/POS values, order and unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
All 50 rows 3251–3300 remain, including both `divers` subclasses. CEFR is unknown.

## Modifications and attribution

One everyday use per group retains four independently reviewed fields.
French definitions adapt selected semantics and remove markup. EN/ZH are newly
written Lexique explanations of the same use. Isolated IPA retains selected
variants; `la plupart` is composed from fixed `la`/`plupart` components.
Lexique contributors receive credit for selection, explanations/adaptations
and source-boundary corrections. The `la plupart` primary binding uses a
short general-majority fragment; `patrouille` support omits historical purpose
prose. [Exact replacements](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-146/accepted-replacements.json) retain both boundaries.

Fixed article/full-history links and the complete contributor registries and
anonymous counts in [source-context.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-146/source-context.json) credit Wiktionnaire
contributors. Registries can extend beyond the fixed revision and do not prove
sentence authorship. Declared DAF8 original-work credits remain separate; the
historical France-specific expiry is not worldwide permission. Actual selected
facts/conventional formulations and contribution rights are assessed in
[selected-rights.md](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-146/selected-rights.md). No article marker supplies blanket
clearance or blanket exclusion.

Selected source material, legal text, attributions, modifications and notices
accompany the reviewed shard. Full raw/API/request captures remain in the
external author/reviewer evidence archives. Historical expressive quotations,
examples and media are not accepted selected material. Downstream adaptations
retain ShareAlike and these applicable notices without additional restrictions.

# Source and modification notices for #147

The fixed Wiktionnaire contribution layer and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations use
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code remains MIT. The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-147/COPYING),
source/history links, contributor records, original-work credits and
modification notices accompany this independently reviewed shard.

Exact word/POS membership and unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Rows 3301–3350 retain their order and grammatical subclasses. CEFR is unknown.

## Modifications

One sense is selected per exact group. French definitions explain the selected
lexical facts; English and Chinese are Lexique explanations,
not upstream bilingual quotations. Gender, number, register and construction
restrictions are retained. IPA selects one recorded isolated variant. Source
spelling bindings add no query aliases. [Accepted fields](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-147/accepted-fields.md)
retain all four fields, selected uses and excluded alternatives. Thirty uses
retain separate minimal factual source fragments; twenty retain individually
reviewed short expressions. Five field texts have exact proposal/acceptance
records in [accepted replacements](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-147/accepted-replacements.json).

## Article credits

Wiktionnaire contributors are credited through each complete linked article
history and the completed named registry/anonymous counts in
[source-context.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-147/source-context.json). The registry may extend beyond the
fixed revision and does not prove sentence-level authorship. Lexique contributors
are credited for selection, French adaptation and new English/Chinese wording.

aliases. [Readable author proposals](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-149/review-candidates.md) are preserved;
[groups.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-149/groups.json) and [field-review.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-149/field-review.json) retain
accepted fields and actual selected/excluded-use decisions.

Independent corrections remove an unsupported internal-location restriction
from Chinese `organe` (row 3407), restrict EN/ZH `choquer` to offence (row 3429),
and restrict FR/EN/ZH `lady` daughters' courtesy rank to dukes, marquesses or
earls (row 3444). These six modified texts and their exact source bases are in
[accepted-replacements.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-149/accepted-replacements.json). The remaining 194
texts are unchanged. Every field passes quality and selected rights review.

Specific historical expression is credited to Académie française, Dictionnaire
de l’Académie française, eighth edition, 1932–1935, where identified in the
34 actual comparisons in [original-expression-review.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/906acc0a477e5d035bc2227e54245b7ae4255416/docs/evidence/issue-149/original-expression-review.json).
This includes unmarked/reference-only articles. Original public-domain expiry
is 2006-01-01 under the established collective-work basis; subsequent wiki
transcription/adaptation and Lexique modifications retain CC BY-SA 4.0.
Modern external dictionary/interface prose is excluded. Article-level
historical expression is not a selected IPA input.

Retain CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text and licence/source identifiers, complete
contributor/history attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification
notices and selected source material. Adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0 without
additional restrictions. External works retain their separate rights.
The coordinator verifies actual combined source materials, notices and
conversion before canonical admission.

All 200 new fields await separate quality and selected-span rights review.
No new field is independently accepted or admitted by this author package.


# Source and modification notices for #150

The fixed Wiktionnaire contribution layer and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations retain
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code remains MIT. The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-150/COPYING),
source/history links, contributor records, original-work credits and
modification notices accompany these independently reviewed selected fields.

Exact word/POS membership and both unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen scope manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Rows 3451–3500 retain their order and grammatical subclasses. CEFR is unknown.

## Modifications

One selected sense is accepted per exact group. French wording is a scoped
adaptation of the selected lexical semantics; English and Chinese are new
Lexique explanations, not upstream bilingual quotations. Construction, gender,
number, register and region restrictions are retained. One recorded applicable
isolated IPA variant is selected. Audio, images, lyrics and literary/news
quotations supply no learner field. Source spelling relationships add no lookup
aliases. [Readable fields](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-150/review-candidates.md) retain every exact field and
the selected and excluded uses.

[Selected rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-150/selected-rights.md) records the established collective-work
basis and its 2006-01-01 expiry. Every selected field has independent review.
The selected `tailler` shaping sentence also matches DAF8 and retains original
Académie credit. `tranquillement` retains original DAF8 and Émile Littré,
*Dictionnaire de la langue française*, credit; Littré's original-work expiry is
1952-01-01. The selected `publicité` commercial-advertisement sentence at line 26
matches DAF8. Original credits remain separate from the CC BY-SA wiki and
Lexique adaptation layers.
The CFC cartographic-letter definition in `capitale` at line 42 is excluded;
the capital-city definition at line 8 is selected. No CFC prose supplies a field or support.

## Redistribution obligations

Retain CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text and licence/source identifiers, complete
contributor/history attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification
notices and selected source material. Adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0 without
additional restrictions. External works retain their separate rights.
The coordinator verifies actual combined source materials, notices and
conversion before canonical admission.

All 200 selected fields pass independent quality and selected-span rights review.
Canonical conversion, combined packaging obligations and native gates remain
coordinator-owned; this shard admits no new canonical field by itself.


# Source and modification notices for #151

The fixed Wiktionnaire contribution layer and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations retain
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code remains MIT. The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-151/COPYING),
source/history links, contributor records, original-work credits and
modification notices accompany these independently reviewed records.

Exact word/POS membership and both unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen scope manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Rows 3501–3550 retain their order and grammatical subclasses. CEFR is unknown.

## Modifications

One selected everyday sense is accepted per exact group. French wording is a scoped
adaptation of the selected lexical semantics; English and Chinese are new
Lexique explanations, not upstream bilingual quotations. Construction, gender,
number, register and region restrictions are retained. One recorded applicable
isolated IPA variant is selected. Audio, images, lyrics and literary/news
quotations supply no learner field. Source spelling relationships add no lookup
aliases. [Preserved authored proposals](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-151/authored/groups.json) retain every exact field and
the selected and excluded uses.

## Article credits

Wiktionnaire contributors are credited through each complete linked article
history and the paginated named registry/returned anonymous counts in
[source-context.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-151/source-context.json). Anonymous identities retain history
attribution. A current contributor registry can extend beyond a fixed revision
and does not identify who authored a selected sentence. Lexique contributors
are credited for selection, French adaptation and the new English/Chinese text.

basis and its 2006-01-01 expiry. All 200 selected fields have separate quality and selected-expression rights decisions.

## Redistribution obligations

Retain CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text and licence/source identifiers, complete
contributor/history attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification
notices and selected source material. Adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0 without
additional restrictions. External works retain their separate rights.
The coordinator verifies actual combined source materials, notices and
conversion before canonical admission.

All 200 selected fields and 50 everyday uses passed separate independent review.
Canonical conversion and native verification are recorded by the coordinator.


# Content notices for independently reviewed issue #152

Selected wiki contributions and Lexique adaptations/translations: CC BY-SA 4.0. See [COPYING](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-152/COPYING) for the complete licence and warranty disclaimer. Retain attributed source links, histories, original-work credits, modification notices and ShareAlike; no additional downstream restrictions. Project code is MIT.

Author proposals and exact accepted replacements are preserved. No audio/media, illustrative quotation, modern publisher sentence or page layout is selected content.

Original DAF8 expressions: Académie française, collective eighth edition (1932–1935), CPI L123-3, conservative expiry 2006-01-01. # Source and modification notices for #153

All 200 independently reviewed fields retain CC BY-SA 4.0 for fixed
Wiktionnaire contributions, scoped French adaptations and new Lexique
English/Chinese explanations. [COPYING](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-153/COPYING) contains the complete licence.
Project source code is MIT; content licences remain separate.

Exact frozen rows 3601–3650 and both unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier, Lexique 3.83, CC BY-SA 4.0, through the
[frozen manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Source: https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html

French definitions adapt one selected use. IPA selects a recorded isolated form
and adds slashes; no sound recording is copied. English/Chinese are new Lexique
explanations. No literary/news quotation, image or publisher definition enters
the fields. vôtres remains bound to les vôtres; volé retains its participle/theft
meaning. No runtime alias is admitted. CEFR remains unknown.

## Original works and modifications

DAF8 original credit: Académie française, Dictionnaire de l’Académie française,
eighth edition (1932–1935), institutional collective edition, expired
2006-01-01 under CPI L123-3. Littré original credit: Émile Littré,
Dictionnaire de la langue française (1872–1877), expired 1952-01-01 under L123-1.
The R:Rivarol original credit is Antoine de Rivarol manuscript material and
quatre professeurs de l’Université, the anonymous compilers of Dictionnaire
classique de la langue française, Paris: Brunot-Labbé and Baudouin frères, 1827.
The anonymous original compilation expired 1898-01-01 under L123-3. Original
author/work respect and wiki/Lexique adaptation credits are retained.
Import/bibliography markers and article credits do not prove sentence authorship.
These findings concern original editions, not modern proprietary transcriptions.

by/NOM retains geography and pond-drainage scope. Its English/Chinese explain
bonde as a drain outlet without requiring a gate. The current publisher page
corroborates use/domain facts only; its definition/example prose is not bundled.
Exact proposals, replacements and source spans are retained in
[accepted-replacements.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-153/accepted-replacements.json) and [authored](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-153/authored/snapshot.json).

# Source and modification notices for #154

The fixed Wiktionnaire contribution layer and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations retain
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code remains MIT. The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-154/COPYING),
source/history links, contributor records, original-work credits and
modification notices accompany this independently reviewed shard.

Exact word/POS membership and both unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen scope manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Rows 3651–3700 retain their order and grammatical subclasses. CEFR is unknown.

## Modifications

One selected sense is retained per exact group. French wording is a scoped
adaptation of the selected lexical semantics; English and Chinese are new
Lexique explanations, not upstream bilingual quotations. Construction, gender,
number, register and region restrictions are retained. One recorded applicable
isolated IPA variant is selected. Audio, images, lyrics and literary/news
quotations supply no learner field. Source spelling relationships add no lookup
aliases. [Authored proposals](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-154/authored/review-candidates.md) retain every exact field and
the selected and excluded uses.

## Article credits

Wiktionnaire contributors are credited through each complete linked article
history and the paginated named registry/returned anonymous counts in
[source-context.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-154/source-context.json). Anonymous identities retain history
attribution. A current contributor registry can extend beyond a fixed revision
and does not identify who authored a selected sentence. Lexique contributors
are credited for selection, French adaptation and the new English/Chinese text.

retain original credit separately from the wiki and Lexique adaptation layers.
[Selected rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-154/selected-rights.md) records the established collective-work
basis and its 2006-01-01 expiry. New fields require their own independent review.

## Redistribution obligations

Retain CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text and licence/source identifiers, complete
contributor/history attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification
notices and selected source material. Adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0 without
additional restrictions. External works retain their separate rights.
The coordinator verifies actual combined source materials, notices and
conversion before canonical admission.

All 200 new fields await separate quality and selected-span rights review.
No new field is independently accepted or admitted by this author package.

## Selected original expressions and reviewed text

The original institutional collective Dictionnaire de l’Académie française,
eighth edition (1932–1935), is separately credited where a selected expression
corresponds to the original edition. The established CPI L123-3 French
original-work calculation expires conservatively on 2006-01-01. This basis
does not license modern electronic editorial content or establish selected
sentence authorship. Fixed Wiktionnaire contributions and Lexique adaptations
remain CC BY-SA 4.0, with the attribution and modification information above.
The exact original quotations and retained original-edition responses are in
[original-expression-review.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-154/original-expression-review.json).

# Source and modification notices for #156

The fixed Wiktionnaire contribution layer and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations retain
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code remains MIT. The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-156/COPYING),
source/history links, contributor records, original-work credits and
modification notices accompany these author proposals.

Exact word/POS membership and both unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen scope manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Rows 3751–3800 retain their order and grammatical subclasses. CEFR is unknown.

## Modifications

The selected shard contains one sense for each of 49 ordinary groups and an
owner-approved zero-field annotation for row 3783 `ya/NOM`, with four missing
fields. [Rejected proposals](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-156/rejected-proposals.json) and [authored records](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-156/authored/groups.json)
retain the slang-knife proposal separately. French wording is a scoped
adaptation of the selected lexical semantics; English and Chinese are new
Lexique explanations, not upstream bilingual quotations. Construction, gender,
number, register and region restrictions are retained. One recorded applicable
isolated IPA variant is selected. Audio, images, lyrics and literary/news
quotations supply no learner field. Source spelling relationships add no lookup
aliases. [Readable proposals](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-156/review-candidates.md) retain every exact field and
the selected and excluded uses.

Articles declaring Académie française eighth-edition imports (1932–1935)
retain original credit separately from the wiki and Lexique adaptation layers.
[Selected rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-156/selected-rights.md) records the established collective-work
basis and its 2006-01-01 expiry. New fields require their own independent review.

## Redistribution obligations

Retain CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text and licence/source identifiers, complete
contributor/history attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification
notices and selected source material. Adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0 without
additional restrictions. External works retain their separate rights.
The coordinator verifies actual combined source materials, notices and
conversion before canonical admission.

All 200 fields and 50 selected-use rights boundaries were independently reviewed.
196 unchanged fields / 49 ordinary groups pass quality and are selected for
scope admission. The [owner decision](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-156/owner-approval.json) of 2026-11-23,
America/Vancouver, approves only the exact zero-field ya annotation; it admits
no rare-slang content, alias or substitution. Four explicit unresolved missing
fields carry that decision. All 200 proposal selected-text rights pass; this
audit does not admit the rejected ya texts. Canonical redistribution remains
pending. See [independent review](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-156/README-independent-review.md).

Mouchoir's fixed source credits inspiration from the Dictionnaire encyclopédique
Quillet (Aristide Quillet, Paris, 1934; direction Raoul Mortier), independently
identified by [BnF FRBNF31164348](https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb31164348q).
The original collective publication term ends 2005-01-01; later editions and
separately authored images are not covered. The DAF9 reference is not permission
to copy its prose. Valet's Quillet 1979 reference receives no blanket clearance:
its selected card expression is independently present in the primary Académie
eighth edition (1935, tome 2 p.705). See [original-work boundaries](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-156/selected-original-work-review.json).


# Source and modification notices for #157

The fixed Wiktionnaire contribution layer and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations retain
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code remains MIT. The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-157/COPYING),
source/history links, contributor records, original-work credits and
modification notices accompany these independently reviewed records.

Exact word/POS membership and both unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen scope manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Rows 3801–3850 retain their order and grammatical subclasses. CEFR is unknown.

## Modifications

One selected everyday sense is accepted per exact group. French wording is a scoped
adaptation of the selected lexical semantics; English and Chinese are new
Lexique explanations, not upstream bilingual quotations. Construction, gender,
number, register and region restrictions are retained. One recorded applicable
isolated IPA variant is selected. Audio, images, lyrics and literary/news
quotations supply no learner field. Source spelling relationships add no lookup
aliases. [Reviewed fields](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-157/review-candidates.md) retain every exact field and
the selected and excluded uses.

Articles declaring Académie française eighth-edition imports (1932–1935)
retain original credit separately from the wiki and Lexique adaptation layers.
[Selected rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-157/selected-rights.md) records the established collective-work
basis and its 2006-01-01 expiry. All 200 accepted fields have separate quality and selected-expression rights decisions.

## Redistribution obligations

Retain CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text and licence/source identifiers, complete
contributor/history attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification
notices and selected source material. Adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0 without
additional restrictions. External works retain their separate rights.
The coordinator verifies actual combined source materials, notices and
conversion before canonical admission.

All 200 selected fields passed separate independent review. Canonical assembly
and packaged combined obligations remain coordinator-owned.

## Selected original-expression boundaries

[Original-expression decisions](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-157/original-expression-review.json) distinguish
matched DAF8 wording, ordinary lexical/grammatical facts and external references.
The accepted `crapaud` meanings use only the DAF8-corresponding frog-resemblance
clause and modern amphibian terminology. Unmatched additions remain
outside the accepted fields and source span. All adapted text retains CC BY-SA
4.0; the full authored proposal remains in [authored](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-157/authored/snapshot.json).


# Source and modification notices for #158

The fixed Wiktionnaire contribution layer and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations retain
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code remains MIT. The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-158/COPYING),
source/history links, contributor records, original-work credits and
modification notices accompany the independently reviewed selected records.

Exact word/POS membership and both unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen scope manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Rows 3851–3900 retain their order and grammatical subclasses. CEFR is unknown.

## Modifications

All 50 frozen groups retain one selected proposal. French wording is a scoped
adaptation of the selected lexical semantics; English and Chinese are new
Lexique explanations, not upstream bilingual quotations. Construction, gender,
number, register and region restrictions are retained. One recorded applicable
isolated IPA variant is selected. Audio, images, lyrics and literary/news
quotations supply no learner field. Source spelling relationships add no lookup
aliases. [Field/use decisions](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-158/field-review.json) retain exact proposed/accepted
text and selected/excluded uses. The complete author package is preserved under
[authored](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-158/authored/README.md.source).

The accepted `g` fields select the fixed French letter-name frame and retain
its masculine invariable nominal use, corroborated by current Académie and
Larousse grammatical facts. The three `pétrin` meanings retain familiar register.
External proprietary definitions are not learner source expression.

## Article credits

Wiktionnaire contributors are credited through each complete linked article
history and the paginated named registry/returned anonymous counts in
[source-context.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-158/source-context.json). Anonymous identities retain history
attribution. A current contributor registry can extend beyond a fixed revision
and does not identify who authored a selected sentence. Lexique contributors
are credited for selection, French adaptation and the new English/Chinese text.

retain original credit separately from the wiki and Lexique adaptation layers.
[Selected rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-158/selected-rights.md) records the established collective-work
basis and its 2006-01-01 expiry. Article-level DAF8 reference markers also retain
conservative original credit for potentially inherited lexical text, separately
from later wiki and Lexique editorial contributions.

## Redistribution obligations

Retain CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text and licence/source identifiers, complete
contributor/history attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification
notices and selected source material. Adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0 without
additional restrictions. External works retain their separate rights.
The coordinator verifies actual combined source materials, notices and
conversion before canonical admission.

All 200 selected-expression rights decisions pass independently. Quality/use
acceptance is 49 groups and 196 fields; four `cm/NOM` fields remain unresolved.
No new field is canonically admitted by this review shard.


# Source and modification notices for #159

The fixed Wiktionnaire contribution layer and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations retain
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code remains MIT. The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-159/COPYING),
source/history links, contributor records, original-work credits and
modification notices accompany the reviewed shard.

Exact word/POS membership and both unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen scope manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Rows 3901–3950 retain their order and grammatical subclasses. CEFR is unknown.

## Modifications

One reviewed sense is selected for each of 48 ordinary groups, totaling 192
fields. Rows 3922 haver/VER and 3944 da/ONO are owner-approved zero-field
annotations with eight missing fields; their complete research proposals remain
in [the rejected ledger](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-159/rejected-proposals.json). All 200 rights audits are
retained, with admission eligibility distinguished in [rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-159/rights.json).
French wording is a scoped
adaptation of the selected lexical semantics; English and Chinese are new
Lexique explanations, not upstream bilingual quotations. Construction, gender,
number, register and region restrictions are retained. One recorded applicable
isolated IPA variant is selected. Audio, images, lyrics and literary/news
quotations supply no learner field. Source spelling relationships add no lookup
aliases. [Reviewed fields](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/2c57f22872c1471a20bcf1d8322c83beb113d347/docs/evidence/issue-159/review-candidates.md) retain every exact field and
the selected and excluded uses. Accepted text explicitly retains living prey and
steak intended for pan cooking; French/EN/ZH adaptations remain CC BY-SA 4.0.

history and the paginated named registry/returned anonymous counts in

attribution. A current contributor registry can extend beyond a fixed revision
and does not identify who authored a selected sentence. Lexique contributors
are credited for selection, French adaptation and the new English/Chinese text.

contributor/history attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification
notices and selected source material. Adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0 without
additional restrictions. External works retain their separate rights.
The coordinator verifies actual combined source materials, notices and
conversion before canonical admission.

The independent review accepts 192 fields across 48 ordinary groups and
retains selected-text rights clearance for all 200 audited texts. Eight research
fields are not admitted; two owner-approved annotations retain their frozen
identities and eight missing fields. Canonical admission remains pending.

## Approved rex annotation

Frozen row 3953 `rex/NOM` is an owner-approved zero-field annotation dated 2026-11-26. Its identity, both 10.57 frequency strings and ordering are preserved; four fields remain missing. [Owner approval](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/15bb7e2fe6c58ee413325b95807a159a011dce07/docs/evidence/issue-160/owner-approval.json) does not resolve the rejected proposal's expression rights or admit a specialist sense. The [rejected proposal](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/15bb7e2fe6c58ee413325b95807a159a011dce07/docs/evidence/issue-160/rejected-proposals.json) and independent decisions remain preserved.


# Issue #161 selected content notices

These 50 groups / 200 fields pass independent selected-field quality, everyday-use, spelling and selected-expression rights review and are admitted in core-162-v1. The integration receipt records their Windows x64 lookup, trusted save and reopen verification.

French lexical adaptations and new English/Chinese explanatory translations: Lexique contributors. Fixed Wiktionnaire transcription and contribution layers, and Lexique adaptations: CC BY-SA 4.0. Retain attribution, source/history links, modification notices and ShareAlike; impose no additional restrictions. The complete legal text accompanies this shard in COPYING.

Original historical layer where declared: Académie française, Dictionnaire de l’Académie française, eighth edition (1932–1935). The established collective-work L123-3 original-work basis expires conservatively on 2006-01-01; later Wiki and Lexique contributions retain CC BY-SA 4.0. Import/reference markers do not identify the author of a selected sentence. The selected expressions pass separate rights review; original-work credit is retained at each inspected boundary in original-expression-review.json.

Only selected lexical definitions, isolated IPA and necessary French/POS/construction evidence supply the selected fields. Literary/news quotations, media, etymologies and other-language sections remain outside the selected resource. The CFC cartographic definition of fidélité at line 40 is excluded. Full API/raw sources are retained separately for inspection.

Frozen membership: Boris New and Christophe Pallier, Lexique 3.83, CC BY-SA 4.0. Exact 50 rows 4001–4050, spelling, grammatical subclass and subtitle frequency strings are retained from the accepted scope manifest. The global denominator remains 4,087 groups.

Modifications: lexical selection, markup removal, scoped French adaptation, new English and Chinese explanations of the same selected French use, and one recorded isolated-headword IPA variant in slashes. No runtime spelling alias is admitted.

## Additional original-work credit

Émile Littré (1801–1881), Dictionnaire de la langue française (1872–1877), for the independently inspected historical expression boundaries of infiniment, épais and quête. The original author-work basis expires conservatively on 1952-01-01 under CPI L123-1. Wiki and Lexique adaptation layers retain CC BY-SA 4.0. No modern XMLittré, ARTFL or CNRTL transcription is admitted.


# Source and modification notices for #162

The fixed Wiktionnaire contribution layer and Lexique’s scoped French
adaptations and new English/Chinese explanations retain
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode.en).
Project source code remains MIT. The [complete legal text](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/15bb7e2fe6c58ee413325b95807a159a011dce07/docs/evidence/issue-162/COPYING),
source/history links, contributor records, original-work credits and
modification notices accompany the reviewed shard.

Exact word/POS membership and both unchanged frequency strings derive from
Boris New and Christophe Pallier’s [Lexique 3.83](https://chrplr.github.io/openlexicon/datasets-info/Lexique383/README-Lexique.html),
CC BY-SA 4.0, through the [frozen scope manifest](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/15bb7e2fe6c58ee413325b95807a159a011dce07/resources/core-pilot-79/scope-manifest.csv).
Rows 4051–4087 retain their order and grammatical subclasses. CEFR is unknown.

## Modifications

One selected sense is eligible in each of 36 groups; ais/NOM retains no
admitted sense. French wording is a scoped
adaptation of the selected lexical semantics; English and Chinese are new
Lexique explanations, not upstream bilingual quotations. Construction, gender,
number, register and region restrictions are retained. One recorded applicable
isolated IPA variant is selected. Audio, images, lyrics and literary/news
quotations supply no learner field. Source spelling relationships add no lookup
aliases. [Readable content](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/15bb7e2fe6c58ee413325b95807a159a011dce07/docs/evidence/issue-162/review-candidates.md) retains every exact field and
the selected and excluded uses.

## Article credits

Wiktionnaire contributors are credited through each complete linked article
history and the paginated named registry/returned anonymous counts in
[source-context.json](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/15bb7e2fe6c58ee413325b95807a159a011dce07/docs/evidence/issue-162/source-context.json). Anonymous identities retain history
attribution. A current contributor registry can extend beyond a fixed revision
and does not identify who authored a selected sentence. Lexique contributors
are credited for selection, French adaptation and the new English/Chinese text.

Articles declaring Académie française eighth-edition imports (1932–1935)
retain original credit separately from the wiki and Lexique adaptation layers.
[Selected rights](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/15bb7e2fe6c58ee413325b95807a159a011dce07/docs/evidence/issue-162/selected-rights.md) records the established collective-work
basis and its 2006-01-01 expiry. Selected-expression rights are independently
reviewed. The explorer DAF8
marker is in the unselected English noun section. Ais/NOM is an owner-approved
zero-field annotation at row 4057; four fields remain missing and its rejected
proposal is preserved separately.

## Redistribution obligations

Retain CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text and licence/source identifiers, complete
contributor/history attribution, applicable original-work credits, modification
notices and selected source material. Adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0 without
additional restrictions. External works retain their separate rights.
The core-162-v1 package contains the matching source materials, notices and
converted resource.

All 148 proposed texts have separate quality and selected-span rights decisions.
The independently accepted 144 fields in 36 groups are admitted in
core-162-v1 with matching combined packaging and Windows x64 native evidence.

The reviewed FR/EN/ZH changes select the normal baseball format with tie
extensions, the stick-guided firework rocket and the current French admiral
rank. IPA is unchanged. Exact text and modifications are recorded in
[accepted replacements](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/15bb7e2fe6c58ee413325b95807a159a011dce07/docs/evidence/issue-162/accepted-replacements.json).


## Approved ais annotation

Frozen row 4057 `ais/NOM` is an owner-approved zero-field annotation dated 2026-11-26. Its identity, both frequency strings and source order are preserved; four fields remain missing. The original proposal and independent rejection of everyday eligibility remain in [rejected proposals](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/15bb7e2fe6c58ee413325b95807a159a011dce07/docs/evidence/issue-162/rejected-proposals.json). [Owner approval](https://github.com/zardonc/lexique/blob/15bb7e2fe6c58ee413325b95807a159a011dce07/docs/evidence/issue-162/owner-approval.json) does not admit a specialist sense or change spelling/POS.
